title: Hyperspectral Satellite-Derived Phytoplankton Diagnostic Pigments in the East China Sea: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Ecological Response to Coastal Fronts
content: Phytoplankton diagnostic pigments are critical for identifying phytoplankton functional types, yet their retrieval is limited by sparse in situ data and low spectral resolution. This study retrieved phytoplankton diagnostic pigments in the East China Sea using hyperspectral PACE ocean color data with 5 nm resolution in the visible range. Fine spectral features from synchronous in situ HPLC–hyperspectral remote sensing reflectance datasets from the ECS and global ocean were extracted via Gaussian decomposition to construct an Optuna-optimized CatBoost model. The model performance was validated against multispectral MODIS-derived results, and its robustness was further verified across independent random and two out-of-distribution generalization scenarios. Results showed PACE/OCI test set ${{R}^2}$ exceeded 0.80 with MAE of 0.2–0.4 and RMSE of 0.3–0.7, comparing to MODIS’s test set ${{R}^2}$exceeded 0.69 with MAE of 0.2–0.7 and RMSE of 0.4–1.1. Monthly average pigment distributions from PACE revealed a spatial pattern of nearshore/offshore high, outer sea low and seasonal trend of winter-spring high and summer low, with regional variations. Case analyses of the Shandong Peninsula and Min-Zhe coastal fronts confirmed that seasonal ocean fronts regulated pigment distribution by acting as nearshore accumulation barriers in winter and promoting blooms in spring. Our study provides a reliable framework for ECS pigment monitoring, supporting coastal ecological assessment, and offers a reference for hyperspectral satellite applications in marginal seas.
author: Han Wang, Fang Shen, Renhu Li

title: DFDSCF: A Dual-Frequency and Dynamic Sparse Cross-Path Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is a challenging task due to the complex spatial–spectral properties and the high-dimensional nature of the data. Existing models still face challenges in simultaneously capturing fine-grained structural details and discriminative spectral patterns, as well as in enabling sufficiently deep interaction between spatial and spectral modalities, thereby limiting their effectiveness in complex scenes. To address these challenges, this article presents a novel dual-frequency and dynamic sparse cross-path fusion network (DFDSCF), which is constructed with three key components: First, a dual-frequency multidirection enhancement module, which utilizes dual-frequency transforms and direction-aware convolutions to capture structural details, mitigating spatial detail loss; Second, a dynamic instance-level sparse channel self-attention module, which employs a multiscale complexity gating mechanism to perform instance-adaptive sparse channel selection, filtering out redundant bands and extracting discriminative spectral features; Finally, a cross-path adaptive fusion (CPAF) module, which leverages CPAF strategies to achieve the deep interaction and integration of spatial and spectral features. Comprehensive experiments on four benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that DFDSCF achieves competitive classification performance, attaining overall accuracies of 99.92%, 99.21%, 99.90%, and 99.90% on the Pavia University, Indian Pines, WHU-Hi-HanChuan, and WHU-Hi-HongHu datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for HSI classification.
author: Xiaoqing Wan, Huilu Tang, Kun Hu, Haibing Yan, Hui Liu, Zhize Li

title: PSMamba: Conditional Multiscale Mamba for Remote Sensing Image Pan-Sharpening
content: Pansharpening combines panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) images to recover high-resolution MS imagery. Many methods treat the two inputs as equivalent feature sources and fuse them by concatenation or addition. This treatment can transfer unwanted high-frequency content from the PAN image and disturb interband relationships in the MS features. We instead regard the PAN image as a spatial constraint and propose PSMamba, an asymmetric conditional guidance framework. Its dynamic spatial filtering mechanism uses Mamba's selective scan to retain useful PAN structures while limiting texture injection. Its conditional spectral calibration mechanism adjusts MS feature distributions under spatial guidance to preserve interband proportions. On the WorldView-II, WorldView-III, and Gaofen-2 datasets, PSMamba improves PSNR over Pan-Mamba by up to 0.89 dB and reduces SAM by up to 6.8%, indicating better spectral fidelity with a controlled spatial-spectral tradeoff.
author: Wangrui Xu, Wentao Yang, Haifeng Li

title: Automated Semantic Segmentation Label Generation for Large-Scale Wetland Mapping Using Local Gaussian-Weighted Reverse K-Nearest Neighbor
content: Wetland mapping is a fundamental prerequisite for ecological conservation and management, yet large-scale applications are severely hindered by the difficulty of acquiring high-quality and low-noise training samples. Manual interpretation is costly, inefficient, and prone to uncertainty, which substantially limits the generalization capability of intelligent mapping models. To address these challenges, this study proposes a highly automated and reliable framework for training sample generation and optimization in large-scale wetland mapping. Ecological index thresholding combined with Mahalanobis distance-based outlier detection is then employed to ensure initial sample reliability. Furthermore, a novel sample selection and relabeling strategy based on a local Gaussian-weighted reverse K-nearest neighbor algorithm is introduced to robustly identify and correct noisy and confused samples by jointly leveraging high-dimensional spectral features and local spatial neighborhood information. Cross-regional generalization experiments conducted across seven ecologically heterogeneous regions demonstrate that the proposed framework yields remarkable performance improvements against initial labels produced by random forest, with the overall accuracy enhanced by 3%–6% and the Kappa coefficient elevated by 4%–10% across all test regions. The proposed approach provides an efficient, robust, and highly generalizable solution for intelligent wetland mapping across diverse regional ecological settings.
author: Junkai Shi, Zhenguo Niu, Jie Wang, Tianjie Zhao, Yaseen Laghari, Xuanlin Huo

title: Adaptive Point Selective Deformable Attention and Multiscale 3-D Convolution Dynamic Fusion for Hyperspectral Band Selection
content: Band selection is an essential way to reduce hyperspectral dimensionality. Due to treating all features equally or relying on fixed single-scale convolutional kernels, most current methods fail to capture complex structures or subtle spectral variations within images, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these limitations, this article proposes an adaptive point selective deformable attention and multiscale 3-D convolution dynamic fusion network. First, an adaptive point selective deformable attention module is designed, which dynamically samples high-value pixels based on spectral similarity and refines their locations through an offset network to better fit the target’s spatial structure, while retaining the original input to include potentially overlooked significant pixels. Second, a multiscale feature extraction and dynamic fusion module is proposed. It employs a multibranch 3-D convolution architecture to extract features at different scales and dynamically learns branch weights according to the input sample, enabling the model to focus on different spectral intervals. During feature fusion, spatial and channel attention mechanisms are utilized to generate adaptive weights to effectively integrate the deformable spatial features and multiscale spectral features. Finally, the information entropy of the reconstructed image is used to assess the value of each band, and the original bands corresponding to the reconstructed bands with high entropy are selected as the candidate set. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches.
author: Jinjin Wang, Jiahang Liu, Xiaozhen Wang, Zhaohui Xue, Fuping Gan

title: RadarDiff: A Conditional Diffusion Model With Time-Aware Context and Mixed Attention for Radar Echo Extrapolation
content: Accurate radar echo extrapolation is essential for precipitation nowcasting. Existing deterministic models suffer from regression to the mean and are prone to oversmoothing, leading to distorted representations of strong convective cores. While generative models provide rich image details, they incur heavy computational overhead and high inference latency. To address these issues, this article proposes a conditional diffusion model named RadarDiff, which achieves a better tradeoff among forecast performance, image quality, and computational efficiency through the synergistic design of three core modules. First, a causal context network incorporating a CausalLSTMCell enhances the motion continuity of radar echoes. Second, a long-range temporal dynamic interaction block combined with a spatial-channel attention mechanism improves the prediction stability of strong echoes. Finally, an adaptive multiscale interaction block utilizing cross-scale feature fusion facilitates capturing the evolution of strong echoes. Experimental results based on a Shanghai radar dataset demonstrate that RadarDiff outperforms deterministic baselines in terms of core metrics, such as critical success index and Heidke skill score, effectively alleviates the oversmoothing problem, and exhibits superior dynamic consistency. Furthermore, compared to existing generative models operating under their default inference configurations, RadarDiff effectively reduces computational overhead and inference latency while maintaining superior forecast accuracy. In summary, RadarDiff provides a balanced and effective solution for generative nowcasting.
author: Huantong Geng, Xinxin Zeng, Liangchao Geng, Han Zhao, Delong Fang, Xiaoran Zhuang

title: Enhancing Target and Rectifying Clutter: A Structure-Guided Frequency Rectification Network for Infrared Small-Target Detection
content: Infrared small-target detection (IRSTD) remains challenging under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, where weak target responses are easily submerged by complex background clutter. Existing enhancement-oriented methods may inadvertently activate target-like clutter in complex backgrounds. Once propagated through feature aggregation, these mixed activations can degrade mask reconstruction and increase false alarms. In multiscale high-frequency representations, target and clutter regions may both produce pronounced responses, but their dominant response locations exhibit distinct behaviors across neighboring scales. Target-related peaks tend to remain close to their reference-scale locations, whereas clutter-related peaks exhibit larger cross-scale displacements. This distinction suggests that weak target enhancement and clutter response rectification should be considered jointly. Accordingly, we propose a structure-guided frequency rectification network (SGFR-Net) for IRSTD. Specifically, a progressive contextual differential enhancement block is designed to strengthen weak local target responses and reduce target attenuation during feature propagation. Since the enhanced responses may still contain target-like clutter, an Edge-Guided Frequency Interaction Refinement module is introduced to refine clutter-contaminated high-frequency representations through edge-guided compact cue selection and cross-scale high-frequency interaction. A Cross-Level Feature Interaction Fusion module further performs selective multilevel aggregation to reduce feature inconsistency during mask reconstruction. Extensive experiments on SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1 K demonstrate that SGFR-Net achieves strong segmentation accuracy and robust detection performance under complex backgrounds.
author: Peng Tu, Chunqiang Sun, Jianjun Liu

title: End-to-End Deep Reconstruction and Clustering of Satellite Image Time Series for Crop Group Mapping
content: Classification of annual crops according to their seasonality (crop group classification) is beneficial for various applications, for instance, drought prevention. Using satellite image time series (SITS) allows access to the temporal patterns that correspond to the phenology of the crops. On one hand, training data for such applications may be scarce, especially when relatively wide scenes are considered, thus prompting the need for unsupervised approaches. On the other hand, optical SITS usually exhibit missing data, e.g., due to clouds. One common practice to address unsupervised classification in SITS with missing values is to perform gap filling prior to the clustering task. The choice of methods for both tasks is often performed independently, which may generally influence the effectiveness of the resulting clustering solution. In this article, we propose a neural architecture that performs gap filling and clustering simultaneously in an end-to-end framework for crop group classification. In comparison to previous deep clustering methods that conduct representation learning and cluster assignment separately, these tasks are also addressed jointly by the proposed approach, together with the gap-filling task. For this purpose, the developed method combines a generative component, based on a conditional generative adversarial network, with an information-theoretic clustering component. Experimental results on two datasets suggest the effectiveness of the proposed method as well as the relevance of all of its architectural components.
author: Priscilla Indira Osa, Gabriele Moser, Sebastiano B. Serpico, Josiane Zerubia

title: Improving UAV-Derived Nearshore Bathymetry Using Geospatial Machine Learning
content: Accurate coastal bathymetry is essential for ocean science and blue economy applications. However, nearshore regions remain undersurveyed due to dynamic environmental conditions and the limitations of traditional multibeam echosounders (MBES). This study presents a framework that integrates high-resolution uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery with geospatial machine learning to address spatial variability in reflectance-depth relationships and to mitigate performance overestimation by explicitly accounting for spatial autocorrelation. The workflow combines exploratory spatial data analysis, spatially explicit model development using the geographical random forest (GRF) algorithm, and comprehensive evaluation through global metrics and local spatial analysis. The framework was applied to a sand-bottom coastal area in southwestern Portugal, using UAV-derived multispectral reflectance as predictors and MBES measurements as ground truth. The GRF model captured spatially varying relationships between spectral bands and depth, outperforming conventional random forest in both predictive accuracy and interpretability, though at a higher computational cost. Spatial analysis indicated that the red band was the most influential predictor at the global scale, while the near-infrared band dominated in shallow areas. The green band proved most relevant within the depth range where predictions were most accurate. Furthermore, the results identified a practical optical depth limit of approximately 5 m in the study area, beyond which prediction reliability rapidly declined due to signal attenuation. These findings indicate that spatially explicit modeling yields improved insight into depth-dependent prediction behavior and feature relevance, supporting more accurate and regionally consistent coastal bathymetric mapping. This framework is reproducible and applicable to other coastal environments.
author: Telmo Dias, Paulo Carvalho, Ana Cristina Costa, Marcia L. Baptista

title: Itoh-Constrained Hybrid Graph Learning With Sparse Supervision for InSAR Phase Unwrapping
content: Phase unwrapping (PU) is a fundamental step in synthetic aperture radar interferometry (InSAR), yet it remains an inherently ill-posed problem due to the $\text{2}\pi$ ambiguity of the interferometric phase. Existing deep learning-based PU methods typically rely on dense pixelwise supervision using absolute phase values, which introduces a fundamental mismatch with the intrinsic structure of PU and often leads to poor generalization. In particular, the mapping from wrapped phase to absolute phase is inherently one-to-many, making pixelwise regression ambiguous and difficult to learn. In contrast, classical PU methods mitigate the ill-posedness by exploiting the Itoh condition, which enforces consistency on phase differences rather than absolute values. This observation suggests that effective supervision for PU should be imposed on phase gradients, i.e., along edges. To this end, we propose an Itoh-constrained hybrid graph (IC-HG) framework, which reformulates PU as an edgewise gradient regression problem using sparse observations. By enforcing the Itoh condition on graph edges, the proposed method ensures physically consistent phase differences and alleviates the ill-posedness of PU. Specifically, IC-HG constructs a weighted hybrid graph, where a global minimum spanning tree guarantees global connectivity and suppresses phase drift, while dynamically sampled local K-nearest neighbor edges capture fine-scale phase variations and prevent geometric overfitting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms dense supervision and other baseline methods under both uniform and nonuniform sampling conditions. Moreover, IC-HG exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability, particularly when only sparse supervision is available, highlighting its effectiveness for real-world InSAR applications.
author: Jialong Gong, Lifan Zhou, Hanwen Yu, Taoli Yang, Wei Liu, Li Cheng, Hao Liu, Xin Ye, Huanghao Feng, Vito Pascazio

title: A Two-Step Machine Learning Framework for High-Resolution Reconstruction of Regional GNSS-Derived PWV Grids Using Meteorological Auxiliary Data
content: High-resolution precipitable water vapor (PWV) gridded products provide essential data for atmospheric state estimation and monitoring of regional heavy precipitation. PWV retrieved from the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) offers high temporal resolution and all-weather observation capability; however, the sparse and uneven distribution of GNSS stations limits its direct application in constructing continuous high-resolution moisture fields. To address this limitation, this study integrates discrete GNSS-PWV observations with high-resolution rapid refresh meteorological information and develops a spatial reconstruction framework to generate PWV grids with a resolution of 0.01$^{\circ }\times$ 0.01$^{\circ }$, enabling high-resolution reconstruction from sparse station observations to a continuous high-resolution water vapor field. First, a light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM)-based PWV spatial interpolation model is developed to generate initial PWV grids. Then, a LightGBM-based bias correction model is constructed using meteorological information to further improve grid accuracy. The results show that PWV spatial interpolation models based on LightGBM, extreme gradient boosting, inverse distance weighting, and ordinary kriging achieve root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.80, 0.84, 1.19, and 1.26 mm, respectively, with LightGBM showing the best performance. The LightGBM-based bias correction model achieves an RMSE of 0.40 mm. For the PWV grids generated during 2022–2024, the RMSEs relative to GNSS-PWV are 0.38, 0.36, and 0.37 mm, respectively. After bias correction, the RMSEs decrease to 0.30, 0.30, and 0.30 mm, corresponding to accuracy improvements of 21.05%, 16.67%, and 18.92%, respectively. In addition, the reconstructed PWV grids exhibit strong spatiotemporal consistency with precipitation processes, effectively capturing water vapor accumulation prior to heavy rainfall events as well as the spatiotemporal evolution of water vapor during precipitation.
author: Huafeng Ma, Biyan Chen, Feiyang Hu, Chaohui Chen

title: M2GCN: A Multiadjacency Mamba-Enhanced Graph Convolutional Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Leveraging the advantage of utilizing both labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data simultaneously, superpixel-based graph convolutional networks (GCN) have garnered widespread attention in the field of hyperspectral image classification. However, existing methods based on GCN primarily rely on single adjacent relationship modeling and do not fully utilize the edge relationships between superpixels, which limits their classification performance in complex terrain scenarios. In addition, GCN mainly focuses on the global dependencies of the entire hyperspectral image, making it difficult to simultaneously consider local dependencies and rich spectral features. To alleviate these issues, in this article, a novel multiadjacency Mamba-enhanced graph convolutional network (M2GCN) for hyperspectral image classification is proposed. First, a hierarchical cascade dimensionality reduction strategy is proposed to efficiently extract features and map them to the superpixel feature space. Second, considering the superpixel edge information, a similarity-edge enhanced GCN module is designed, which explicitly encodes superpixel adjacency constraints and guides the propagation of superpixel features with structural awareness. Finally, a new spectral-Mamba guided convolutional neural networks branch is constructed to decouple the extraction process of spatial local features and spectral information, and to recalibrate the channel weights. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, compared to the state-of-the-art method, M2GCN achieves classification performance improvements of 1.63%, 1.40%, and 1.29% on the Indian Pines, Pavia, and WHU-Hi-LongKou tasks, respectively.
author: Cuiping Shi, Chaowei Xia, Weiwei Sun, Chenyang Fu, Zhan Jin

title: Mitigating False Positives in Complex Spectral Scenarios: A Mutual Information Guided Wavelet Disentanglement Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) constitutes a fundamental task for quantifying spatiotemporal variations on the Earth’s surface through bitemporal image analysis. Despite significant advances in deep learning methodologies, existing approaches often exhibit persistent limitations in complex scenarios characterized by intricate grayscale variations, particularly manifesting as elevated false positive rates in edge and shadow regions where illumination artifacts obscure genuine change signatures. To systematically address these challenges, we propose ACNet, a graph-enhanced adaptive wavelet transform network with cross-layer knowledge injection and mutual information regularization. The proposed framework integrates an adaptive wavelet decomposition with graph convolution module that combines discrete wavelet transforms with graph neural networks in non-Euclidean space to comprehensively capture multiscale frequency-domain features while modeling complex spatial relationships; a mutual information regularization mechanism that encourages latent cross-subband decoupling and reduces interfrequency redundancy, thereby minimizing interfrequency redundancy and enhancing discriminative feature representations; and a dual-temporal differential feature complementation and alignment module that performs sophisticated multiscale feature integration through bidirectional cross-attention mechanisms, ensuring optimal fusion of fine-grained spatial details with high-level semantic information. Extensive experiments on five widely-used benchmark datasets demonstrate that ACNet consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods, capable of detecting both subtle and large-scale changes while substantially mitigating false positives in challenging scenarios with complex spectral variations.
author: Daobo Sun, Xiaodong Zhang, Zhe Yang, Xiangxu Meng, Baoqiang Zhang

title: COWVR Wind Direction Performance for One-Look Versus Two-Look Viewing Geometry
content: The Compact Ocean Wind Vector Radiometer (COWVR) instrument is a technological demonstration of a compact, low-cost polarimetric microwave radiometer for measuring wind speed and direction over the ocean surface. COWVR’s internal calibration system enables Earth observations over the entire scan and a two-look wind direction retrieval. When we compare COWVR’s two-look wind directions with retrievals that use only one of COWVR’s looks, we find that certain relative wind directions are prone to error in one-look retrievals. These include: 1) relative wind directions that correspond to the extrema of the 3rd and 4th Stokes wind direction emissivity model (near $45^{\circ }$, $135^{\circ }$, $225^{\circ }$, and $315^{\circ }$) where there are clusters in the frequency of data, and 2) downwind observations around $180^{\circ }$ for the lowest chi-squared ambiguity which have skill rates of $20 \,\%$ to $40 \,\%$ and root-mean-square errors (RMSE) versus ERA5 up to $45^{\circ }$. When we compare COWVR’s one-look and two-look retrievals with NCEP and ERA5 model winds, CCMP, ASCAT-C, and moored buoys, we find that the one-look RMSE for the lowest chi-squared ambiguity is $33^{\circ }$ in low winds ($3\,\,{\mathrm{to}}\,\, 9 \,\mathrm{m}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{s}$) and $19^{\circ }$ at high winds ($15\,\,{\mathrm{to}}\,\, 21 \,\mathrm{m}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{s}$), whereas the two-look error is $22^{\circ }$ in low winds and $7^{\circ }$ in high winds. The two-look lowest chi-squared wind direction RMSE is within $1^{\circ }$ of the closest wind direction to a comparison dataset, which indicates that the two-look algorithm is optimally performing without having to use an ancillary wind direction dataset. In addition, the lowest chi-squared wind direction RMSE of the two-look retrieval is about $3^{\circ }$ to $4^{\circ }$ lower than the closest RMSE of the one-look retrieval. Due to the diversity of relative wind directions when both looks are available, the two-look capability significantly improves the wind direction retrieval.
author: Katherine Nelson, Richard Lindsley, Thomas Meissner, Carl Mears

title: ISGM: An Illumination-Aware Semantic-Guided Mamba Network for RGB–Infrared Vehicle Detection in UAV Imagery
content: RGB–infrared (RGB-IR) vehicle detection in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is essential for applications, such as traffic monitoring and object tracking. However, existing methods often suffer from heterogeneous feature responses across modalities, degraded RGB feature representations under adverse illumination, and insufficient capture of fine-grained structural and edge details, which collectively impede accurate cross-modal modeling and localization. To alleviate these issues, we propose an Illumination-aware Semantic-Guided Mamba (ISGM) network. First, we design a Feature Representation Refinement module that stabilizes RGB and IR features through scale-specific channel remapping and normalized nonlinear refinement, yielding more reliable representations for subsequent cross-modal interaction. Furthermore, to enhance robustness to illumination variations and better preserve detailed structural cues and boundary information, we develop a cross-modal feature interaction mechanism comprising the Illumination-Aware Fusion Modulation (IAFM) module and the Detail-enhanced Semantic-Guided Mamba (DSGM) module. Specifically, the IAFM module estimates illumination-aware modality reliability weight maps, thereby improving robustness under challenging illumination conditions. These weight maps guide the DSGM module to integrate high-level semantic information and low-level detail cues into multiscale guidance features. These features are subsequently used to modulate the scanning parameters for adaptive RGB-IR feature interaction. This design improves the modeling of target-region features while minimizing interference from complex backgrounds. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle and VEDAI datasets demonstrate that ISGM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in detection performance while achieving a favorable accuracy-efficiency balance among comparable methods.
author: Jinyu Liu, Ming Li, Yuli Sun, Lin Lei, Gangyao Kuang

title: Decoupling Clutter Suppression and Target Localization: A Two-Stage Framework for Robust Radar Detection
content: Complex sea clutter remains a major challenge for radar target detection because of its non-Gaussian statistics, heavy-tailed fluctuations, and pronounced nonstationary behavior, which severely degrade the reliability of weak-target detection. Existing deep learning methods usually perform clutter suppression and target localization within a single-stage framework, where the two objectives are optimized simultaneously in a shared feature space. However, these two objectives are inherently conflicting in clutter-dominated radar observations: aggressive clutter suppression may oversmooth weak target responses, whereas excessive preservation of local target-like structures may retain clutter spikes and increase false alarms. To address this problem, we propose a two-stage framework that explicitly decouples clutter suppression from target localization. In the first stage, a sequential clutter representation network (SCR-Net) treats radar echoes as sequential representations and suppresses structured sea clutter by modeling its long-range spatial dependencies. In the second stage, a target-aware spatial refinement network (TSR-Net) takes the channelwise concatenation of the original radar image and the clutter-suppressed output as input, and focuses on target-oriented spatial refinement and localization. By separating global clutter modeling from local target localization, the proposed framework alleviates the representation conflict between background attenuation and weak target preservation. Extensive experiments on both physically realistic simulated datasets and real radar measurements demonstrate that the proposed method achieves stronger clutter suppression, higher detection reliability, and superior computational efficiency compared with representative traditional detectors and deep learning baselines. These results indicate that task decoupling provides an effective and practical solution for robust radar target detection in complex sea clutter environments.
author: Zhengyang Yi, Yucheng Jiang, Ziqiang Wang, Jun Cao, Yongfeng Zhi, Jun Zhang, Xiwen Yao

title: A Graph-Based Inference Framework for Active Landslide Identification by Integrating InSAR Data and Landslide Prior Knowledge
content: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables large-area observation of ground surface deformation and has become an important technique for identifying active landslides. However, deformation detected by InSAR is not exclusively caused by landslide activity, engineering activities, agricultural disturbance, land subsidence, and other nonlandslide processes may also produce similar deformation signals. As a result, existing deep learning methods that rely only on InSAR-derived features are prone to false identification in complex environments. To address these issues, this study proposes a graph-based inference framework for active landslide identification by integrating InSAR with landslide prior knowledge to distinguish landslide-related deformation candidates from other deformation signals. First, an improved Yolov11n-based detection model is employed to extract candidate deformation areas from InSAR data. Subsequently, a topological graph is constructed using joint constraints of spatial proximity and environmental similarity, thereby explicitly encoding the spatial-environmental relationships among different deformation candidates. In this process, each detected deformation area is treated as a node, and ten categories of landslide influencing factors related to terrain, geology, hydrology, and human activities are assigned as node attributes. Finally, a graph neural network-transformer model is employed to perform node-level inference by integrating local graph connectivity with multihop contextual information, thereby distinguishing landslide-related deformation from nonlandslide deformation. Experiments conducted in the Bailong River Basin suggest that the proposed framework improves the discrimination of landslide-related deformation candidates. The results indicate that incorporating landslide prior knowledge into graph inference can reduce the risk of false identification caused by nonlandslide deformation and provide a feasible technical pathway for constructing regional-scale active landslide candidate inventories.
author: Huaiyuan Chen, Yi He, Haowen Yan, Hui Zhang, Wenhui Wang, Jinkun Yang, Fei Gao, Qing Zhang, Lifeng Zhang, Youdong Chen, Chunlin Huang

title: Synchronization-Free Backdoor Attacks on Edge-Deployed Neural Network for IoT Systems
content: Deep Neural Networks integrated into sensor-driven embedded systems have become fundamental to edge computing applications. While Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) are ubiquitous in these architectures due to their cost-efficiency, the reliance on data-driven models expands the attack surface of the embedded computing pipeline. This paper investigates the vulnerability of such systems by presenting a synchronization-free backdoor attack framework. We address two critical threat models in the system lifecycle: training-data poisoning and outsourced training. For the poisoning setting, we exploit the physical-digital signal interface by developing a frequency-domain injection method that utilizes sidelobe perturbations to implant stealthy triggers. For the outsourced scenario, we propose a dual-optimization joint trigger learning scheme that co-optimizes trigger patterns and model objectives, eliminating the dependency on synchronization with the victim’s training process. To ensure attack stealthiness within the operational bounds, a dynamic weighting strategy is introduced to balance attack efficacy with benign inference accuracy. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that current embedded architectures are highly susceptible to these methods: the frequency-domain poisoning achieves over 60% average attack success, while the outsourced-training attack exceeds 95%, highlighting a critical security gap in sensor-based intelligent systems.
author: Bing Zhang, Lei Xie, Kaixuan Zhang, Qixuan Cai, Xin Xie, Xiaoyi Tao, Xu Hu, Xiulong Liu

title: HIGH: Harnessing GPU Parallelism for Optimized HQC Performance
content: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC) was a candidate algorithm in the fourth round of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standardization process and was ultimately selected as a standardized cryptographic scheme in the latest round. To date, although HQC has been optimized for FPGA, CPU, and other platforms, research on GPU-based parallel acceleration remains significantly underexplored. Given this, our research aims to investigate the feasibility and efficiency of hand-optimized HQC implementations on GPU, addressing the current research gap in GPU-based implementations of code-based cryptographic algorithms. In this paper, we introduce a High-performance Implementation of GPU-based HQC, named HIGH. First, we propose a novel architecture for coding-based PQC implementations, significantly reducing redundant global memory access through core fusion. Second, we design a HIKD structure for HIGH, combining a high-order multiplication scheme (HIK) and a low-order multiplication scheme (HID), achieving an impressive 85.6% improvement over Official fourth round Optimized Implementation. Third, through extensive experimentation, we sought the optimal HIKD combination and identified the optimal parallel parameters, leveraging these optimizations, HIGH surpasses current state-of-the-art benchmarks, with Key Generation, Encapsulation, and Decapsulation performance increased by 20$\times$×, 32$\times$×, and 39$\times$×, respectively.
author: Jiankuo Dong, Yuze Hou, Shiqin Wang, Letian Sha, Fu Xiao, Zhenjiang Dong, Jingqiang Lin

title: GACER-M: Granularity-Aware and Memory-Centric Coordination for Multi-Tenant Deep Learning
content: Multi-tenant computing, which executes multiple neural networks on a single GPU, is essential for maximizing hardware utilization in both cloud and edge environments. However, effective co-location faces a fundamental trade-off between utilization and safety. On one hand, the diverse computing patterns of concurrent models lead to resource fragmentation, requiring fine-grained scheduling to improve throughput. On the other hand, modern workloads (especially Generative AI) introduce strict memory constraints: their dynamic memory growth requires rigid reservation to prevent Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes, often leaving valuable resources idle but inaccessible to other tenants. Existing solutions struggle to balance these two sides: static partitioning ensures safety but limits utilization, while aggressive fine-grained scheduling boosts speed but risks system instability. To address this, we propose GACER-M, a unified resource coordination framework that harmonizes fine-grained computing with strict memory governance. Unlike previous approaches that sacrifice speed for safety, GACER-M achieves the best of both worlds via a tiered strategy: (1) A granularity-aware spatial mechanism that minimizes computational residue via operator splitting, strictly regulated by a cost-benefit guardrail to prevent memory bloat; (2) A memory-driven temporal coordination technique that segments dynamic workloads to safely inject concurrent tasks into resource gaps. GACER-M consistently achieves 1.35$\times$×$\sim$∼1.67$\times$× speedup in compute-bound scenarios compared to state-of-the-art works; furthermore, in memory-critical scenarios, it delivers 1.33$\times$× higher effective capacity and 1.4$\times$× aggregate throughput while ensuring strict memory safety.
author: Yongbo Yu, Fuxun Yu, Jiaqi Yang, Xiuzhen Cheng, Chenchen Liu, Xiang Chen

title: SpinTran: A Spintronic Transformer Accelerator Using Full-Precision Computing in Memory With Approximate Softmax Functions
content: Transformer models have made remarkable contributions to various artificial intelligence (AI) applications. However, high energy consumption and delay caused by matrix multiplication (MM) and softmax are bottleneck for hardware to implement transformer models. Computing in memory (CIM) is a promising architecture to solve these problems by reducing data movement and enabling highly parallel data processing. In this work, we propose a software-hardware co-design SpinTran accelerator using the full-precision spintronic CIM and approximate softmax functions for performing energy-efficient transformer models. First, a full-precision CIM scheme (FPCIM) based on toggle spin torque magnetic random-access memory (TST-MRAM) is proposed to realize fast MM operation. Second, we build a highly-reconfigurable array by utilizing the characteristic of TST-MRAM, which can write multiple bits into a column simultaneously to significantly reduce write-back cycles for dynamic matrix in transformer models. Third, we design an efficient Taylor expansion method that adopts approximation and range reduction techniques to achieve rapid convergence, thereby improving the computational efficiency of softmax function. Results show that the delay and energy efficiency of the proposed SpinTran accelerator are 3.5 ns and 56.7 TOPS/W in INT8 MAC operation, respectively. Meanwhile, the energy consumption is 4.71 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$μJ/token, 12.82 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$μJ/token, and 4.32 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$μJ/token when executing Bert-base, Bert-large, and ViT-small models, respectively, which achieves 2.81 to 4.30$\boldsymbol{\times}$× energy reduction compared to other state-of-the-art works.
author: Bojun Zhang, Zhengkun Gu, Ziyuan Guo, Zekun Wang, Jinkai Wang, Weisheng Zhao, Yue Zhang

title: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training With Pipelining Optimization
content: Sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has emerged as a key technique to expand the size of Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) while maintaining low computational costs. However, MoE layers require to route the input data to distributed devices, incurring significant communication latency. Existing studies have primarily focused on alleviating this problem by overlapping computation and communication tasks within a single MoE layer, which fails to achieve sufficient overlap and results in limited performance gains. In this work, we introduce an orthogonal partitioning dimension from existing task-parallel methods by leveraging the autoregressive nature of causal Transformer-based LLMs, i.e. partitioning tasks along the sequence dimension. This provides more flexible and efficient overlaps among tasks from both non-MoE and MoE layers. To this end, we propose an efficient MoE training approach, SP-MoE, with two innovative designs. 1) It incorporates non-MoE layers into the overlapping with not only the current MoE layer but also the preceding MoE layer, thereby facilitating more efficient training; 2) It identifies the optimal combination of pipeline degrees for non-MoE and MoE layers and devises the best scheduling plans for load-imbalanced non-MoE and uniform MoE layers to achieve the goal of minimizing the total training latency. Furthermore, we extend our algorithm to incorporate pipeline parallelism (PP) for training larger MoE models, which introduces peer-to-peer (P2P) communications between adjacent PP stages. To mitigate this problem, we propose S3P-MoE with two optimizations: 1) it partitions P2P communication into chunks and each P2P chunk is transmitted immediately to be overlapped with expert computation; 2) it allows the subsequent PP stage to commence upon receiving the corresponding P2P chunk. Moreover, we refine our algorithm to jointly optimize pipeline degrees for both MoE and non-MoE layers, as well as P2P communication, to minimize overall training latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SP-MoE and S3P-MoE effectively identify optimal pipeline degrees, reducing training time by up to $34.3\%$34.3% and $30.61\%$30.61%, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art methods.
author: Ne Wang, Wenxiang Lin, Lin Zhang, Shaohuai Shi, Ruiting Zhou, Bo Li

title: AMARETTO, Accelerating Quantum Algorithm Development With FPGA Emulation
content: In recent decades, Quantum Computing (QC) has gained widespread attention among researchers and industries, driven by its potential to outperform classical systems in several key areas. However, validating novel quantum algorithms poses substantial challenges due to limited qubit availability and noise in current quantum devices. Although software simulators are frequently employed to validate quantum circuits, they are time-consuming and require high memory availability since as the number of qubits increases, the memory occupation grows exponentially. Hardware emulators have recently emerged as a faster, more efficient, cost-effective alternative. This article introduces AMARETTO (quAntuM ARchitecture EmulaTion TechnOlogy), a new architecture designed to improve quantum computing emulation on resource-constrained Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). To provide a flexible and complete tool for quantum algorithm development, the emulator supports two universal gate sets, Clifford+T and rotational. AMARETTO mimics quantum computing’s inherent parallelism through multiple concurrent processing elements, achieving high throughput by harnessing the sparse nature of the gate matrices, coupled with pipelining in a Reduced Instruction Set Computer (RISC)-like architecture. A dedicated compiler translates OpenQASM 2.0 into AMARETTO’s instructions, enabling support for custom gates leveraging the equivalences known in the literature. Experimental results on an AMD Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC ZCU106 demonstrate successful emulation of quantum circuits up to eighteen qubits with a throughput of $\mathbf{12.207}\frac{\mathbf{kgates}}{\mathbf{s}}$12.207kgatess, validated against Qiskit simulators. Our evaluation confirms competitive performance with existing FPGA-based emulators in terms of throughput and scalability, while targeting an affordable FPGA platform.
author: Christian Conti, Deborah Volpe, Mariagrazia Graziano, Giovanna Turvani

title: Revisiting Preemptive Buffer Management for Modern Datacenter Switch Chips
content: Modern high-speed datacenter switch chips rely on on-chip shared packet buffers to absorb transient traffic bursts. Effective buffer management (BM) is therefore critical: BM schemes dynamically allocate shared buffer space across queues to maintain high utilization and low loss under bursty workloads. In this paper, we argue that the convergence of shallow buffers and intense traffic bursts demands a highly agile BM mechanism that can rapidly adjust allocations as congestion evolves. However, existing BMs are fundamentally constrained by their non-preemptive nature: they primarily depend on natural queue draining to reclaim buffer space, which is often too slow at modern line rates and burst timescales. This paper revisits preemptive buffer management, historically viewed as impractical in hardware, and demonstrates that it is now feasible on contemporary switch chips. We introduce Occamy, a preemptive BM design that exploits otherwise idle memory bandwidth to actively reclaim over-allocated buffer space and redistribute it to newly congested queues. Testbed experiments and large-scale simulations demonstrate that Occamy improves end-to-end performance by up to $\boldsymbol{\sim}$∼44%.
author: Danfeng Shan, Jinchao Ma, Jinyu Wang, Yunguang Li, Yuxuan Li, Zeyu Liang, Zicheng Xu, Hao Li, Zhenxing Zhang, Nan Li, Wanchun Jiang, Fengyuan Ren

title: HierSat: Hierarchical Aggregation for Latency-Efficient Federated Learning in Satellite Networks
content: The global coverage of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites creates a natural platform for distributed intelligence, but privacy risks caused by massive transmission of raw remote sensing data pose critical challenges. To address this, federated learning (FL) has become a promising distributed learning framework for satellite networks, which exchanges only model parameters instead of raw data. However, most existing frameworks fail to fully exploit the structure of the satellite networks. Some work using ground stations (GSs) as parameter servers (PS) cannot handle large model parameter transmission due to limited communication windows between LEO satellites and GSs, while others do not effectively use inter-satellite links (ISL) for global model aggregation, thus resulting in significant training latency. Different from existing frameworks, this paper proposes a hierarchical FL framework for satellite networks, HierSat, which strategically leverages the persistent wide-area coverage and stable energy supply of geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) satellites for continuous model synchronization, while harnessing high-speed ISLs to enable direct satellite coordination. Meanwhile, to efficiently leverage the ring communication topology of LEO orbits, the Ring All-Reduce algorithm is adopted for model aggregation. Furthermore, a joint optimization problem addressing master satellite selection, computation resource allocation, and quantization bits is formulated to minimize per-round latency under energy constraints and accuracy requirements. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of HierSat in DNN based classification tasks under satellite networks.
author: Jian Zhou, Wenkai Ji, Yanmeng Wang, Anfeng Liu, Qian He, Fu Xiao

title: ZCRAID: When Zones Meet Blocks—A Heterogeneous RAID Design to Slash Mapping Table Memory
content: Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs have attracted considerable attention from both academia and industry due to their ability to eliminate block-layer taxes in conventional block-addressable SSDs. To realize the vision of large-scale ZNS SSD deployment within a single server, recent studies have proposed log-structured RAID architectures that employ an indirection layer to hide the append-only access semantics of ZNS devices. However, this indirection layer introduces significant challenges in managing large-scale mapping tables: approaches based on fine-grained mappings (e.g., 4 KB) incur excessive memory usage, whereas coarse-grained mappings (e.g., 64 KB) suffer from severe write amplification when handling small updates. To address this trade-off, we first analyze the cloud storage traces. The analysis reveals that while the traffic attributed to fine-grained updates is non-negligible, the associated data occupies a relatively small capacity compared to the overall address space. To utilize this finding, this paper proposes ZCRAID, a heterogeneous RAID architecture that integrates Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs with conventional block-interface SSDs. In ZCRAID, ZNS SSDs are organized as RAID5 to provide an area of large capacity to handle large, aligned write operations with out-of-place updating, while conventional SSDs of a relatively smaller capacity form a RAID1 (or RAID10) array to absorb small in-place updates, thereby offloading mapping management and garbage collection overheads to the block-addressable SSD area. Meanwhile, the architecture introduces an access-pattern-aware data migration policy to synergistically exploit the strengths of each storage area and achieve efficient resource management. Experiments demonstrate that ZCRAID achieves performance on par with existing log-structured RAID solutions while reducing the mapping table memory footprint by up to 4×.
author: Jialin Liu, Mengyang Ma, Yumiao Zhao, Yaqi Li, Dincui Yu, Liang Shi, Edwin Hsing-Mean Sha

title: HDQAtt: A Photonic Transformer Accelerator via Hierarchical Dynamic Precision Quantification
content: While Transformer-based models have achieved remarkable breakthroughs across various domains, their substantial computational and energy costs limit their deployment in practical systems. Recent photonic accelerators have begun exploring Transformer acceleration by mapping computations into the optical domain. However, existing designs primarily focus on how to efficiently implement Transformers and lack optimizations such as quantization and sparsity. This stems from two challenges: (i) fine-grained mixed-precision execution is difficult in fixed-function photonic circuits with limited DAC/ADC resolution, and (ii) dynamic sparsity is hard to exploit because photonic tensor cores are tailored for dense, fixed-size matrices. To address these challenges, we propose HDQAtt, an algorithm-architecture co-designed photonic accelerator that aims to reduce redundant computations to accelerate Transformers. At the algorithm level, we introduce a hierarchical dynamic-precision quantization scheme to dynamically compute token importance at runtime and adaptively allocate token-wise precision levels. At the architecture level, HDQAtt integrates a cross-stage approximation engine and a configurable dynamic-precision tensor core to efficiently support both mixed-precision execution and dynamic sparsity in the optical domain. The comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that HDQAtt achieves an average 1.82$\boldsymbol{\times}$× speedup and 1.92$\boldsymbol{\times}$× energy improvement over the state-of-the-art photonic accelerator while maintaining comparable model accuracy.
author: Xiaofeng Zou, Limingrui Wan, Ziqian Zeng, Huiping Zhuang, Mingkui Tan, Cen Chen

title: ProMit: Proactive Drive Failure Mitigator for Enterprise Storage Systems
content: The exponential growth of data in recent years has heightened the demand for reliable storage solutions to prevent the severe consequences of data loss, predominantly caused by drive failures. Traditional reactive failure tolerance mechanisms result in longer recovery times, higher operational costs, and degraded performance, while these failures continue to occur frequently. Recent research has shifted toward proactive methods that predict failures before they happen. However, most existing studies primarily rely on offline learning models, which are slow to update and lack adaptability to evolving failure patterns. While some studies explore online learning models for driving data streams, these approaches face challenges in scalability and accuracy as data volumes grow. Moreover, no prior work has developed a real-time metric for predicting drive health without the need for model training. Also, there is no proposed solution for mitigating drive failures in the previous work. Additionally, the patterns and root causes of premature failures in NVMe SSDs have remained uncharacterized until now. To address these challenges, we analyze field data from NVMe SSDs in Alibaba data centers, identifying root causes of drive failures and presenting seven key findings. Notably, we find that the average $\frac{WAF}{PowerOnTime}$WAFPowerOnTime, which represents premature drive failure rates in failed drives, is 10.2$\times$× higher than in healthy ones. Given its strong predictive power, we establish this metric as a real-time indicator for drive failure prediction and health status classification—eliminating the need for model training. Based on this insight, we propose a proactive framework to mitigate premature drive failures, which dynamically recommends the best-candidate drives for incoming write requests through continuous monitoring and real-time updates of drive health status. Our framework is non-intrusive and can be implemented within the software stack or back-end storage controllers. Trace-driven analysis of 692,195 NVMe SSDs shows that the proposed framework can project a 40% reduction in premature drive failures and a 6.7× extension of drive lifespan.
author: Mehdi Moradi, Hossein Asadi

title: FedNereus: Incentive-Aware Heterogeneous Federated Learning Under Resource Constraint
content: As public concern about data privacy continues to grow, federated learning (FL), as a machine learning technique that does not require the disclosure of user raw data, has attracted widespread attention. However, it still has many common problems. The first problem stems from the absence of incentive mechanisms utilized to incentivize more participation to improve the performance of learning models. The second problem arises from the limited resources of mobile devices that can be utilized for model training, which will seriously decrease the performance of learning models. To address the aforementioned issues, in this paper, we propose a novel incentive-aware collaborative construction of heterogeneous Federated learNing under resource constraint, namely FedNereus. In fact, FedNereus incentivizes more workers to participate in model training by applying an auction-based incentive mechanism. It is proved that FedNereus allows participating workers to report their actual cost as their bidding price, which is referred to as truthfulness. Furthermore, it also allows workers to obtain non-negative reward, which is also referred to as the individual rationality. In order to break the resource limitation, FedNereus meticulously designs the rules of model selection so that workers can only train a portion of the learning model based on their limited hardware capabilities, while maintaining the performance guarantee of learning models. The excess empirical risk of FedNereus is shown to be upper bounded by $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{T})$O(1T), where $T$T is the number of training rounds. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted, whose results show that FedNereus outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in different learning tasks.
author: Fuyuan Xia, Chenhao Ying, Xikun Jiang, Weiting Zhang, Haiming Jin, Jie Li, Yuan Luo

title: Pushing the Limits of Computing: Transistor-to-Processor Benchmarking at 77 K With Self-Heating Effect
content: Owing to increased power density with each newer technology node, transistors suffer from increased Self-Heating (SH) at room temperature, which is a daunting challenge for circuits and processors’ reliability. Given the increasing interest in leveraging cryogenic temperatures to enhance the performance and energy efficiency of computing systems, understanding SH effects at cryogenic temperatures is critical for the reliability and optimization of such systems. This work presents a comprehensive investigation of SH effects from the transistor to the processor level on the advanced 5 nm FinFET node under cryogenic conditions, specifically at 77 K. Further, it presents a pioneering comparison of SH effects between 5 nm FinFET and 28 nm FDSOI transistors at 77 K. Our findings reveal that FinFET devices on bulk substrate, despite their 3D-confined structure and reduced scale to extreme 5 nm, exhibit better thermal characteristics compared to FDSOI devices at 77 K. This is primarily attributed to the inherent design of FDSOI devices, where the buried oxide layer acts as a thermal barrier, thereby significantly restricting heat dissipation. Further, we explore the standard cell libraries and a processor core operating at 77 K with and without i) SH effect and ii) scaled parasitic resistance using 5 nm FinFETs. The exploration undertaken in this study not only demystifies the thermal behavior of a cutting-edge 5 nm technology under extremely low temperatures but also establishes a new paradigm in selecting technologies for future high-performance computing applications at cryogenic temperatures. It opens new avenues for the development of more efficient and reliable computing systems, paving the way for future innovations in cryogenic computing.
author: Shivendra Singh Parihar, Florian Klemme, Anirban Kar, Yogesh Singh Chauhan, Hussam Amrouch

title: SD-Acc: Accelerating Stable Diffusion through Phase-Aware Sampling and Hardware Co-Optimizations
content: The emergence of diffusion models has significantly enhanced the capabilities of generative AI, leading to improved quality, realism, and creativity in image and video generation. Among these, Stable Diffusion (StableDiff) has become one of the most influential diffusion models for text-to-image generation, serving as a critical component in next-generation multi-modal algorithms. Despite their advances, StableDiff imposes substantial computational and memory demands, affecting inference speed and energy efficiency. To address these hardware performance issues, we identify three key challenges: 1) intensive and potentially redundant computation. 2) heterogeneous operators involving both convolutions and attention mechanisms. 3) widely varied weight and activation sizes. Thus, we present SD-Acc, a novel algorithm and hardware co-optimization solution: At the algorithmic level, we observe that high-level features exhibit high similarity in certain phases of the denoising process, indicating the potential of approximate computation. Therefore, we design an adaptive phase-aware sampling framework to reduce the computational and memory requirements. This general framework automatically explores the trade-off between image quality and algorithmic complexity for any given StableDiff model and user requirements. At the hardware level, we introduce an address-centric dataflow to facilitate the efficient execution of heterogeneous operators within a simple systolic array. The bottleneck of nonlinear operations is comprehensively solved by our novel 2-stage streaming computing and reconfigurable vector processing unit. We further enhance hardware efficiency through an adaptive dataflow optimization that incorporates dynamic reuse and fusion techniques tailored for StableDiff, leading to significant memory access reduction. Across multiple StableDiff models, our extensive experiments demonstrate that our algorithm optimization can achieve up to 3 times reduction in computational demands while preserving the same level of image quality across various models. Together with our highly optimized hardware accelerator, our approach can achieve higher speed and energy efficiency over CPU and GPU implementations.
author: Zhican Wang, Guanghui He, Hongxiang Fan

title: G1Stack: A Learning-Assisted Scheduler Framework for Interactive and Batch Workload Co-Location With High Resource Efficiency
content: Interactive services typically over-provision CPU resources to meet Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for tail latency amidst workload fluctuations. This inefficiency motivates emerging research into workload co-location, where batch jobs are hosted alongside interactive services to harvest underutilized resources. However, the Linux Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) limits potential resource efficiency gains. CFS’s fairness-oriented design lacks support for workload-specific scheduling policies and is unable to simultaneously enforce performance isolation while facilitating fine-grained resource sharing across co-located workloads. Therefore, we present G1Stack, a scheduler framework designed for workload co-location. Specifically, G1Stack incorporates: (1) A parallel dual-policy architecture that schedules latency-critical (LC) tasks from interactive services and best-effort (BE) tasks from batch jobs separately, guaranteeing responsiveness for the former while enhancing computational throughput for the latter; (2) A learning-assisted load-balancing approach that dynamically interleaves LC and BE tasks across cores with fine-grained temporal and spatial distribution to optimize resource efficiency; (3) Integrated workload-aware auto-scaling and load-shedding mechanisms to minimize latency during up-scaling under load spikes, ensuring system responsiveness under dynamic workloads. Stress-testing results demonstrate that G1Stack reduces the non-productive resource ratio to at most 7.55% and shortens the average completion time of co-located batch jobs by up to 62.45% compared to baselines.
author: Dishi Xu, Fagui Liu, Bin Wang, Xuhao Tang, Qingbo Wu, C. L. Philip Chen

title: Miresga: Achieving High-Performance and Reliable Layer-7 Load Balancing With Programmable Switches
content: As online cloud services continue to scale, ensuring both performance and reliability in layer-7 load balancing has become increasingly critical. Programmable switches offer Tbps-level packet processing with limited flexibility, making them promising yet constrained candidates for accelerating layer-7 load balancing. We present Miresga, a hybrid layer-7 load balancing framework that achieves high performance and reliability through software–hardware co-design. Miresga offloads elephant flows to programmable switches for line-rate forwarding, while front-end servers handle protocol parsing and scheduling, ensuring flexibility. To address the limited memory of the programmable switch, Miresga introduces an eBPF-based back-end agent to manage sequence synchronization. Miresga also employs a distributed RDMA-based state synchronization mechanism for failure tolerance and dynamic traffic migration. Our prototype on a 3.2 Tbps Intel Tofino switch demonstrates up to 3.9$\mathbf{\times}$× throughput improvement and 60$\mathbf{\%}$% latency reduction over optimized software baselines, while maintaining stable throughput during front-end server failures and recoveries.
author: Xiaoyi Shi, Ying Liu, Lin He, Yifan Yang, Jiasheng Zhou, Rongbang Wu, Jinlong E

title: Achieving Predictable Timer Management Under Varying Workload Conditions in ROS 2
content: ROS 2 has become a widely adopted framework for developing modular and distributed robotic systems, enabling the construction of complex processing chains that are typically triggered by periodic timers and interconnected through message-passing callbacks. While prior research has focused on analyzing end-to-end latency, little attention has been paid to the workload release mechanisms, particularly the behavior of timer-triggered processing chains under varying system loads. This gap is critical, as improper handling of timer activation can compromise real-time guarantees. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of timer management in ROS 2 executors and reveals key limitations in their ability to satisfy the timing needs of two distinct classes of processing chains: non-skippable chains that demand strict periodic release, and skippable chains that can tolerate instance dropping. To address these shortcomings, we propose a new timer management mechanism that decouples activation, scheduling, and release control. Our approach provides reliable release control for non-skippable chains while adaptively shedding load from skippable ones. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed design significantly improves predictable system performance across diverse and dynamic workload conditions.
author: Yichen Liu, Xu Jiang, Nan Guan, Yue Tang, Shaoshuai Zhang

title: Continuous Bayesian Machine Learning for High-Dimensional Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Yield Analysis and Optimization
content: Traditional yield analysis for analog and mixed-signal (AMS) circuits relies heavily on Monte Carlo (MC) methods, which suffer from a fundamental information inefficiency: they reduce rich, continuous circuit performance metrics to binary pass/fail indicators. As process variations scale into high-dimensional spaces with advanced technology nodes, this inefficiency creates an insurmountable computational barrier. This paper proposes a Continuous Bayesian Inference framework that fundamentally transforms circuit yield analysis from discrete counting to probabilistic integration over the performance landscape. We introduce a Sparse Gaussian Process (SGP) model augmented with Deep Kernel Learning (DKL) to effectively capture the non-stationary correlations in high-dimensional variation spaces, reducing the computational complexity from $\mathcal{O}\mathbf{(}\boldsymbol{n}^\mathbf{3}\mathbf{)}$O(n3) to $\mathcal{O}\mathbf{(}\boldsymbol{nm}^\mathbf{2}\mathbf{)}$O(nm2). Furthermore, we propose an information-theoretic active learning strategy based on convolutional entropy, which exploits the smoothness of circuit performance to optimally select samples that maximize uncertainty reduction. Experimental validation on benchmark circuits, including a 569-dimensional SRAM column, demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves a 34.30$\mathbf{\times}$×-320.14$\mathbf{\times}$× end-to-end speedup over standard MC. Furthermore, compared to state-of-the-art yield analysis baselines, it demonstrates 1.0$\mathbf{\times}$×–5.24$\mathbf{\times}$× end-to-end speedup. Additionally, SBYA can be seamlessly extended to yield optimization tasks, delivering comparable or even superior optimization efficacy while consuming merely one-quarter of the simulation budget required by existing methodologies.
author: Jing Kou, Zidong Chen, Saiya Wang, Liang Zhang, Jiayi Sun, Wang Kang, Wei W. Xing

title: RTB+: Efficiently Mining Configuration-Routing Causality for Heterogeneous Routers
content: Vendor-provided router images hide detailed routing-protocol implementation code, making it challenging to implement the same routing protocol on heterogeneous devices, as well as to locate and repair the configuration errors. While some works attempt to address these issues, they often fail in large-scale deployment due to various challenges, such as vast and complex configurations, difficulty in mining causal relationships, and challenges in describing and applying causal relationships. To solve these problems, we propose RTB+, a novel tool to mine the causality between network configurations and routing behaviors, in order to assist operations personnel in better pinpointing configuration errors. First, RTB+ generates test cases based on configuration features using a coverage-guided combinatorial testing algorithm. Then, RTB+ employs a differential simulator model to obtain differential datasets storing the correspondence between configurations and routing behaviors. Finally, RTB+ constructs multilayer causal graphs to reason about routing behavioral semantics and vendor-level behavioral differences exposed by the underlying execution environment, enabling three key applications: behavioral change identification, configuration error localization, and configuration logic analysis. Experimental results show that RTB+ requires approximately half of the test cases generated by Metha, while improving code coverage by 10%. Moreover, RTB+ mines configuration-routing causal relationships with an accuracy of 98%, which is 5% more efficient than existing tools. Additionally, RTB+ enhances configuration error localization efficiency by an order of magnitude with causal graphs, and can analyze configuration logic within milliseconds.
author: Bocheng Liang, Fuliang Li, Tangzheng Xie, Zhenbei Guo, Haozhi Lang, Qiang He, Chengxi Gao, Xingwei Wang, Jiannong Cao

title: Facilitating Fuzzing-Based Simulation Testing of Autonomous Driving System Through Inter-Vehicle Interaction Modeling
content: The complexity and safety-critical nature of autonomous driving systems (ADS) require rigorous testing to ensure their reliability, especially when handling rare and complex driving scenarios. In response to this demand, fuzzing-based simulation testing has emerged as an important complementary technique for the safety assessment of ADS. It works by continuously mutating the initial driving scenarios (e.g., adding new surrounding vehicles) in a simulated environment, so as to generate previously unknown driving scenarios for ADS testing. However, existing fuzzers put limited emphasis on the modeling and mutation of realistic and diverse inter-vehicle interactions. Hence, they could merely generate uncomplicated or unrealistic driving scenarios, significantly hurting the credibility of the testing results. To address this issue, we propose ISFuzz, a simulation-based ADS fuzzing framework that enables realistic inter-vehicle interactions, to generate more realistically critical driving scenarios. To be specific, ISFuzz enhances conventional fuzzing-based simulation testing with the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) and customized Dynamic Game Model (DGM). Firstly, the IDM, as a vehicle-following model, unambiguously describes the dynamics of the positions and velocities of each NPC vehicle, helping generate realistic inter-vehicle interactions and avoid meaningless NPC-responsible accidents during testing. Secondly, the customized DGM incorporates the concept of social value orientation into inter-vehicle interactions, flexibly generating diverse driving behaviors (e.g., aggressive or conservative) of NPC vehicles. Through extensive experiments on Autoware (i.e., industry-grade high-level ADS), ISFuzz demonstrates high effectiveness in ADS safety assessment. Experimentally, within the same testing time, compared to existing tools, ISFuzz can identify 3.75X more realistic ADS-responsible accident scenarios, meanwhile significantly eliminating unrealistic NPC-responsible ones.
author: Wanqi Zhang, Kanye Ye Wang, Xiaobo Zhou

title: Vivisecting the Dissection: On the Role of Trusted Components in BFT Protocols
content: A paper by Gupta et al. (EuroSys ’23) challenged the usefulness of trusted component (TC) based Byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT) protocols to lower the replica group size from $3f + 1$3f+1 to $2f + 1$2f+1, identifying three limitations of such protocols and proposing that TCs should be used instead to improve the performance of BFT protocols. Here, we point out flaws in both arguments and advocate that the most worthwhile use of TCs in BFT protocols is indeed to make them as resilient as crash fault-tolerant (CFT) protocols, which can tolerate up to $f$f faulty replicas using $2f + 1$2f+1 replicas.
author: Alysson Bessani, Miguel Correia, Tobias Distler, Rüdiger Kapitza, Paulo Esteves-Verissimo, Jiangshan Yu
